The stays of the Chinese monk Yijing in Srivijaya, the trading kingdom on Sumatra, on his way to India and back between 671 and 695.

Yijing sailed from Guangzhou on a merchant ship in 671 and spent about six months in Srivijaya learning Sanskrit grammar before going on to India. There he studied for years at Nalanda, the great Buddhist university. On the way home he lived in Srivijaya again for several years, copying and translating texts.

He wrote that Srivijaya had more than a thousand monks and advised Chinese pilgrims to study there before going on to India. His writings are among the earliest records of the kingdom, whose wealth came from controlling the Strait of Malacca between China and India.

He returned to Luoyang in 695 and was welcomed by the empress Wu Zetian. He followed the path of Xuanzang and, earlier, Faxian, but by sea.
sum: The stays of the Chinese monk Yijing in Srivijaya, the trading kingdom on Sumatra, on his way to India and back between 671 and 695.
